source.title_on_document: Overreliance in Writing Tasks: Exploring Similarity-Based Measures of AI Influence on Writing and Proposing a Reflective Writing Interface Intervention

supplement.where: Appendix A, 'Task Prompts and AI Suggestions', PDF pp. 17-18; referenced on p. 6, Section 3.4. No separate external supplement is identified in the document.
supplement.holds: Analytical and creative task prompts and the fixed AI suggestions used in the main experiment; no additional statistical tables.

paper_design_summary: Prolific crowd-workers read O. Henry's 'After Twenty Years' and wrote an analytical response and a creative rewrite, receiving a fixed AI suggestion on one task and none on the other; task order and AI assistance were counterbalanced, but random allocation is not stated, and 47 of 54 recruited people were analyzed after 7 exclusions. Outcomes measure each response's similarity to the task-specific AI suggestion (lexical, structural, semantic, and sentiment alignment); a separate think-aloud study with 4 university students evaluated a reflective writing interface. A time-limited pilot with 5 participants and an untimed iteration with 11 participants informed the design only and supplied no reported outcome estimates (PDF pp. 5-11, Sections 3-4; pilot: p. 6, Section 3.3).

studies.label: Main experiment (analysis and creative writing tasks with and without an AI suggestion)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Which of the two tasks came with the AI suggestion, and task order; each participant had one AI-present and one no-AI task
assignment.quote: task order and AI assistance were counterbalanced (Latin-square style). Participants faced an AI suggestion on at least one task, with the order of exposure varying between participants.

arms.name: AI-present trial
arms.description: Task completed with a fixed AI suggestion shown in a side panel: a full direct answer for the analytical task, a scaffold of key points and structure for the creative task

arms.name: No-AI trial
arms.description: Task completed without a suggestion; response scored against the same held-out task suggestion as a counterfactual baseline

participants.exclusions: 7 participants were excluded after data collection for using external tools, leaving 47 analyzed from 54 recruited. The 54 is a recruitment count, not a stated randomized count (PDF p. 6, Section 3.4; external-tool screening: p. 5, Section 3.2).
participants.who: Prolific crowd-workers reporting English fluency and at least secondary-level education; 54 recruited, 7 excluded after data collection for using external tools, 47 analyzed. Each of the 47 appears in both arms (within-person), so 47 people in total.
participants.quote: We recruited a total of 54 participants on Prolific. After data collection, we excluded 7 participants who used external tools, resulting in 47 valid participants.

ai_tool.name_model: Not named in the text; the Fig. 1 screenshot labels the suggestion panel 'GPT 4.5'
ai_tool.how_used: A fixed AI suggestion, reviewed by the research team before the study, was displayed beside the text editor; participants were told not to use external LLMs (p. 5-6, Sections 3.2 and 3.4; Appendix A)

task.description: Two tasks on O. Henry's 'After Twenty Years': an analytical essay judging Bob's decision to wait (direct-answer suggestion), and a creative rewrite of the final scene from Jimmy Wells's point of view (scaffold suggestion)

outcomes.name: Jaccard similarity between the participant's response and the task's AI suggestion (adoption of AI text, not creativity or cross-person diversity)

contrasts.reported: Overall, paired-samples t-test: No-AI 0.093 (SD 0.031) vs AI 0.108 (SD 0.038); Δ = 0.015, p = 0.050, Cohen's dz = 0.294. Within task (independent t-test): analytical 0.104 (0.023) vs 0.128 (0.029), p = 0.003, d = 0.900; creative 0.082 (0.034) vs 0.087 (0.035), p = 0.582, d = 0.162

eligibility.reason: The main experiment analyzed 47 people after 7 exclusions from 54 recruited, below the 50-person threshold (PDF p. 6, Section 3.4). The same 47 people completed both an AI-assisted and an unassisted task, so the two arm counts cannot be added (PDF p. 10, Section 4.1). Task order and AI assistance were counterbalanced, but random assignment or randomized order is not stated (PDF p. 6, Section 3.4; p. 9, Section 4). Outcomes compare each response with the task-specific AI suggestion, measuring AI-text adoption rather than creativity or diversity across writers; criterion 3 fails and context_class remains none (PDF pp. 6-8, Section 3.4; p. 13, Section 5). The pilot iterations report 5 and 11 participants and were used only for design development, with no reported outcome estimates; these counts must not be added to the main experiment (PDF p. 6, Section 3.3). The think-aloud study has 4 university students and an illustrative qualitative analysis (PDF p. 9, Section 3.5; p. 11, Section 4.2).

one_line_finding: With 47 Prolific participants, seeing an AI suggestion raised the similarity of responses to that suggestion (Jaccard 0.108 vs 0.093, p = 0.050; aspect sentiment match 0.092 vs 0.040, p = 0.004; SBERT 0.676 vs 0.642, p = 0.086), mostly in the analytical task (p. 10, Table 1; p. 11, Table 2).
